messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: pagerduty page fired for service=redwood-gpu-alloc (sev=high) — group=kvcache-pools, signal=CUDA_OOM_RATE spike. link: https://pd.local/p/incident/INC-1769995432

pagerduty-bot: Alert escalated to on-call (rotation: eng-oncall). Auto-ack window 2m. If unacked -> escalate to tlead.

alex: acked. I'm looking at the pool metrics now. seeing surge of alloc failures in west2a/gpu-pool-7.

morgan: +1 I see the same in dashboard (token throughput unchanged but mem-fails up). KVCACHE evictions spiked.

sre-bot: auto-shedder engaged on pool "gpu-pool-7". Eviction policy: low-priority preempt, prefetched-kv disabled.

alex: logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-15T03:45:22Z] cuda: CUBLAS alloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T03:45:22Z] runtime: alloc retry -> 0x0
[2026-03-15T03:45:23Z] kvcache: prefetch queue growth 1024 -> 5120
```

alex: initial hypothesis: kvcache prefetch burst + slightly degraded driver in that host group -> fragmentation -> OOMs. Could be a bad prefetch pattern from a model rollout.

devon: checking recent deploys — I have a canary for model: opt-6B-quant that changed prefetch batch size 2h ago. Rolling back canary might help.

sasha: customer impact check: dedicated customers in west2a seeing elevated 5xx on generation routes, ~0.6% of requests returning 503 in last 5m. Also a small spike in latencies for hosted chat.

lia: updating PD notes: INC-1769995432 — GPU OOM surge west2a influencing model-serving. Oncall alex investigating. scc=start investigation.

morgan: I can flip kvcache prefetch global flag to conservative mode for pool-7. That should reduce prefetch IO and lower eviction churn. Want me to do it?

alex: yes please. Do it as a scoped change for pool-7 only. Command: `rdctl pool update gpu-pool-7 --kvcache-prefetch=conservative`

morgan: running:
```
$ rdctl pool update gpu-pool-7 --kvcache-prefetch=conservative --who=morgan
Applying change to pool-7... OK
```

sre-bot: change applied. kvcache prefetch policy now: conservative on gpu-pool-7. Expect reduced prefetch within 30s.

alex: telemetry: eviction rate dropping, alloc-fail rate trending down (5m avg dropped from 120 -> 30). Good sign.

devon: still seeing some residual OOMs from certain hosts (gpu-7-12, gpu-7-14). I'm going to cordon those two nodes for now to let workloads drain: `infractl node cordon gpu-7-12,gpu-7-14 --reason "OOM suspected driver instability"`

morgan: cordon ok, evicting pods. Workloads should shift to other pools/fallbacks.

alex: re: customer impact — contact list: dedicated customers A and B had retries/failures. Reached out to support to open incident tickets and notify them. No major data loss, requests were retried.

sasha: signal from PD: if OOMs stop in next 15m we treat as mitigated; otherwise escalate to infra lead for driver-level rollback.

lia: I'm preparing post-incident checklist. Need: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations done, impacted customer list, suggested long-term fixes (prefetch throttles, better node prewarming).

devon: noticed driver log snippets with nonmonotonic GPU mem reporting on gpu-7-14 prior to OOMs. Putting a note: possible driver regression 532.21 -> 532.23.

alex: plan: 1) keep kvcache conservative for pool-7 for 2 hours; 2) keep nodes cordoned until driver logs stable; 3) roll back opt-6B canary if we see recurrence.

morgan: rollback initiated for canary (opt-6B-quant) on west2a traffic split -> 0%.

sre-bot: rollback completed. Canary removed.

alex: alloc-fails down to near baseline. I'll keep monitoring for next 30m then handoff to night oncall. If metrics hold, I'll close the PD incident.

sasha: thanks team. Handoff note for night oncall (@sasha): watch gpu-pool-7, nodes gpu-7-12/14 cordoned, kvcache conservative, opt-6B canary removed. If OOMs return -> escalate to infra-lead + open driver rollback runbook.

morgan: leaving a small dampening rule: add temporary alert suppress for repeated identical OOM alerts for 10m to avoid noisy PD flapping while we stabilize.

lia: updated PD notes and support messages. Draft customer message ready for review in #support-drafts.

alex: closing steps: will update the postmortem template with timeline and attach logs. If anyone sees a spike, ping directly. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-1769995432 status -> acknowledged by alex at 2026-03-15T03:46:05Z. If not resolved by 2026-03-15T04:01:05Z, will escalate to infra-lead.

sre-bot: monitoring: alloc-fail rate stable < 10/min. Continuing observation.

alex: handing off to @sasha at 2026-03-15T04:02:00Z. I'm available on call if needed.

sasha: thanks alex — taking over. Will keep watch for 3h and open follow-up if we see any driver anomalies.

lia: incident closed (mitigated) in PD — will convert ticket to postmortem workflow.

morgan: quick note for follow-ups: add a canary metric for kvcache prefetch queue length and a hard cap to avoid runaway prefetching.

alex: agreed. filing follow-up tasks in infra backlog. Good job team.
